description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, b2-29: an ISO timestamp came out "2026-01-05T00:00:00Z").  PRE-EXISTING: the emission is identical at v0.1.0, 4429126a, ab4da8b4, 337f6a23 and main 268d7e00 (checked with `git archive` extractions) -- NOT caused by #1923.

REPRODUCERS (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/slice-args1.pl, ctxleak1.pl, ctxleak2.pl + .perl.out / .pcl.out):
  my @g = (5, 4, 3);  sub pair { (1, 2) }  sub ctx { wantarray ? "L" : defined(wantarray) ? "S" : "V" }
  my $a = sprintf "%02d:%02d:%02d", @g[2, 1, 0];          perl 03:04:05     PCL 05:00:00  (+ "Missing argument in sprintf")
  my $d = sprintf "%d/%d", @h{qw(x y)};                   perl 1/2          PCL 2/0
  my $f = sprintf("%s,%s,%s", (localtime(0))[5, 4, 3]);   perl 70,0,1       PCL 1,,
  my $a = sprintf("%s-%s", pair());                       perl 1-2          PCL 2-
  my $b = sprintf("%s", ctx());                           perl L            PCL S        the same for pack("A1", ctx()), die ctx(), warn(ctx()), printf $fh ("%s", ctx())
  my $s = "x" . sprintf("%s-%s", pair());   sub fmt { return sprintf("%s-%s", pair()) } my $t = fmt();   1 ? sprintf(...) : "";   lc(sprintf(...));   if (sprintf("%s%s", pair()) eq "12")      all WRONG the same way
  sub r { return (ctx(), "z")[0] } my $x = r();           perl L            PCL S
  my $o = sprintf("%s-%s", reverse two());                perl b-a          PCL b-       (the leak reaches a NESTED list operator)
RIGHT today: `print sprintf(...)`, `my ($x) = sprintf(...)`, `{ k => sprintf(...) }` (the call itself is in LIST context, so nothing leaks), `join`, `push`, `reverse` at top, `lc(join ...)`, user-sub / coderef arguments, `[...]`, `{...}`, `(LIST)[i]` on the RHS of an assignment.

THE EMISSION: `my $a = sprintf("%d-%d", @g[0,1])` -> `(p-sprintf "%d-%d" (p-list-scalar (p-aslice @g 0 1)))`; `sprintf("%d-%d", f2())` -> `(p-sprintf "%d-%d" (p-scalar-ctx (pl-f2)))`; `(localtime(0))[5,4]` -> `(p-aref-deref ... (progn 5 4))`.
THE MECHANISM (read, Pl/PExpr.pm ~5275-5340, the funcall arm of the node-context function): argument context is decided by HAND-WRITTEN NAME LISTS -- `map|grep|sort|keys|values|each`, `join`, `push|unshift|splice|reverse`, `chop|chomp`, `print|say`, `scalar`, the named unaries -- and a builtin in none of them INHERITS its parent's context.  `sprintf`, `pack`, `die`, `warn`, `printf` (and by the same reading `unlink chmod chown kill utime system exec formline syscall sprintf-likes ...`) are in no list.  Pl/ExprToCL.pm ~2804 has the run-time half as one more name test ("join always evaluates its list arguments in list context" -> ctx_bind t).

FIX SHAPE (rule 11 -- ONE source of truth, not a longer name list): a builtin's argument context is a fact of its PROTOTYPE, and the compiler already carries a MEASURED builtin prototype table (DECIDED "The VALUES are always measured": `prototype("CORE::name")` over cproto.t's names): every argument at or after the first `@` slot is LIST context (`sprintf` = `$@`, `pack` = `$@`, `die`/`warn`/`unlink`/`chmod`/`kill`/`utime`/`chown` = `@`, `formline` = `$@`, `syscall` = `$@`, `push`/`unshift` = `\@@`, `join` = `$@`, `reverse` = `@`, `splice` = `\@;$$@` ...); `$`/`_`/`;$` slots stay SCALAR (that is what the named-unary arm already says by hand).  Builtins with NO prototype (`print`, `printf`, `system`, `exec`, `sort`, `map`, `grep`, `return`, `chomp`/`chop` -- read the comment there on why chomp has no table entry) keep an explicit arm, but ONE table, not six regexes.  The existing hand lists must come out EQUAL to what the table says for the names they cover -- measure that equality first (a script over the table vs the six lists) and list every disagreement in the task BEFORE changing behaviour; then the run-time half (`ctx_bind`) reads the same fact, and the `join` name test goes.  `return (LIST)[i]` and the list-slice index list `(progn 5 4)` are the same leak on a different node type -- probe whether the prototype arm fixes them or they need the listslice arm's own rule (a list slice's LIST and INDEX list are ALWAYS list context, whatever the slice's own context).
PROBE THE CASES THIS WOULD BREAK: a `$`-slot argument that must STAY scalar (`sprintf($fmt_array[0], ...)`: the FORMAT slot -- perl: `sprintf(@a)` uses scalar(@a) as the format!  probe `my @a = ("%s-%s", 1, 2); sprintf(@a)` = "3"), `pack` template slot, `push @a, scalar(f())`, `die` with an object (one arg, must stay the object), `warn` with no args, `unlink` with no args (= `$_`), `kill 0, @pids`, `reverse` in SCALAR context (`my $r = reverse("ab", "cd")` = "dcba": the ARGUMENTS are list context, the RESULT is scalar -- both hold), `print sort { } @x` unchanged.

BAR: a CONTEXT-ANNOTATION change in Pl/ => corpus-diff WILL show many diffs: every differing site explained in CLASSES (a site whose list argument is a plain scalar/literal is textually unchanged; a site that moves had a list-returning call or a slice in a scalar-context sprintf/pack/die/warn -- each class probed vs perl, and each such corpus/lib/board site was SILENTLY WRONG before: LIST them, they are the prize), `tools/emission-ab.pl` over lib + the CPAN board, gen bump + the three artifacts, the FULL sweep (the sweep IS the gate for a context change; expect UPWARD movers in sprintf.t / pack.t / die.t-family rows -- a row that arrives is not a new failure), companion `--quick` once, bench A/B on the rows with sprintf in a hot loop (`strcat`/`textproc`/`sprintf`-style rows: a `p-list-ctx`/`ctx_bind` wrapper around a hot sprintf must not cost; FLAG > 2 %), guard file Pl/t/list-arg-context-01.t with the tables above, INVERSE-verified.


=== DONE (s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
SHIPPED in commit "#2004: a core builtin's argument context is a fact of its PROTOTYPE, not of the
call's own context", plus two follow-ups in the same batch (see below).

WHAT REPLACED WHAT: `Pl::PExpr::child_context`'s six hand-written name regexes are gone.  The one
reading is `Pl::PExpr::Config::core_arg_context`, which asks the running perl for
prototype("CORE::NAME") (the same authority the runtime's %pcl-core-prototypes is built from):
LIST at and after the first slurpy slot (@/%), SCALAR for $ / _ / + / *, inherit for a reference
slot (\@, \%, &).  The builtins perl gives NO prototype are ONE explicit table beside it
(print say printf system exec chop chomp split eval defined).  The map/grep/sort arm STAYS -- it
answers a STRUCTURAL question (which child is the list), not a context one.  The run-time half
(Pl/ExprToCL.pm's `join` name test -> ctx_bind t) reads the same fact.

THE DISAGREEMENT TABLE, taken BEFORE any behaviour changed (118 names, scratch/s492b/proto-disagree.txt
+ proto-disagree-interesting.txt):
  inherit -> LIST      25 slots   THE BUG FAMILY (sprintf pack die warn printf system exec chmod
                                  chown kill utime formline syscall tie ...)
  inherit -> SCALAR   101 slots
  inherit/SCALAR -> SCALAR-glob 38
  LIST -> SCALAR        2 slots   splice's OFFSET and LENGTH ($$), which the old push/unshift/
                                  splice/reverse regex made LIST
  inherit -> ref       16 slots   (no change)
  past-the-end         47 rows
Where the old lists DID fire they disagreed with perl in two places: `reverse` is (@), slurpy from
argument 0, and the rule started at argument 1 (`reverse sort @x` ran the sort in SCALAR context);
splice as above.

THE PRIZE (the sites that were silently wrong): corpus-diff 18 of 111 files, every one a
correction -- list-slice index lists, seek/read/chdir whence and filehandle slots that were LIST or
even VOID, printf argument lists that were VOID, substr/index/unpack/vec scalar slots, reverse's
argument 0.  emission-ab over lib + the CPAN board + shapes: 430 files, 16 DIFF, 0 RCDIFF, all the
same classes.  Logs: scratch/s492b/log-corpus-diff-m1*.txt, log-emission-ab-m1.txt.

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3: slice-args1, ctxleak1, ctxleak2b and tl1 (core Time::Local's timegm per
month -- the acceptance row) now identical; break1's 30 breaking cases unchanged except join's
separator, which becomes correct.  battery2's b2-29 (the ISO timestamp) moved to identical.

TWO FOLLOW-UPS IN THE SAME BATCH:
 (a) die/warn CONCATENATE their FLATTENED list (commit "#2004 residue ...", found by Fable's review
     while the batch ran).  Giving them LIST context made the ARGUMENTS right; the MESSAGE was still
     built from unflattened values, so `die "a", @arr[0,1], "\n"` said `aARRAY(0x1)`.  They now use
     p-flatten-args, the flattener `print` has always used (rule 11), applied BEFORE the
     single-reference test so `die $obj` still throws the object.
 (b) a list slice in SCALAR context is its LAST SELECTED ELEMENT (commit "#2004 follow-up ..."),
     caught by the full sweep: perl-tests/array.t test 31, `$foo = ('a'..'f')[0,2,4]` -- perl 'e',
     this tree '3' before the wrap.  Before #2004 that row passed BY ACCIDENT, on a `(progn 0 2 4)`
     whose value was the last INDEX, which happened to select the same element.  One p-list-scalar
     wrap in gen_array_ref_access_form, gated on the slice marker + non-lvalue + the node's own
     SCALAR context (p-list-scalar is identity on a non-vector, so a single-index slice is
     untouched).  array.t back to its blessed 171/15.

NORMATIVE: docs/ir-spec.md 4.1 (and 3.2e for the slice's own result).
GUARD: Pl/t/list-arg-context-01.t, 13 rows; 10 of the first 11 fail on a 5ce155cb extraction.
RESIDUE FILED: #2030 -- an AGGREGATE LEAF ignores its annotated SCALAR context, so `sprintf(@arr)`
says ARRAY(0x8) where perl says "2".  The CONTEXT is already right; the safe fix is a collapse in
the funcall ARGUMENT loop gated on core_arg_context's own $/_/+ verdict, NOT a generic leaf-level
collapse (a `push @a, ...` reference slot inherits SCALAR and would be collapsed).
subject: SILENT WRONG (everyday, pre-existing since at least v0.1.0): the SCALAR context of an assignment / concatenation / condition LEAKS INTO THE LIST ARGUMENTS of `sprintf`, `pack`, `die`, `warn`, `printf FH (...)` and a `return (LIST)[i]` -- `my $s = sprintf("%02d:%02d:%02d", @t[2,1,0])` formats the slice's LAST element only ("05:00:00"), `my $s = sprintf("%s-%s", pair())` calls pair() in SCALAR context ("2-"), the canonical `sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d", (localtime)[5,4,3])` is wrong; `join`, `push`, `reverse`, `print`, user subs and anonymous constructors are right
